chunks: And glorify Him in the night and when the stars begin to wane.

key_terms.إِدْبَارَ: Setting, waning, or going away (referring to the stars)
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: The night, specifically referring to the time of night prayer
key_terms.فَسَبِّحْهُ: So glorify Him (imperative form directed to the believer)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of glorifying God when the stars wane?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse is often linked to the Prophet Muhammad and the Imams, who utilized the time of 'idbar an-nujum' (the setting of the stars) for deep contemplation and night prayer (Salat al-Layl). This specific timing marks the transition from the night to the dawn, serving as a spiritual threshold for believers to detach from worldly distractions and prepare for the day's duties through sincere devotion.
